stories.title: HKIS paid substantial amount to US church co-founder to end ‘bad marriage’: source

en.title: HKIS paid substantial amount to US church co-founder to end 'bad marriage': source
en.summary: Hong Kong International School reached an out-of-court settlement with the Lutheran Church-Missouri Synod, its US church co-founder, to end their partnership. The church group had sued the school over alleged breach of operating agreement.

stories.title: China bets on early port and power deals in Sudan to secure post-war economic edge

en.title: China bets on early port and power deals in Sudan to secure post-war economic edge
en.summary: China is pursuing port and power infrastructure agreements with Sudan's army-backed government during the ongoing conflict, positioning itself for a significant role in the country's post-war reconstruction.

en.title: China-Russia fishing competition promotes cultural and sports exchanges through fishing friendship
en.summary: The second China-Russia fishing competition and gourmet event took place in Heihe, with participants from both nations demonstrating their fishing skills and engaging in cultural exchange activities.

en.title: Second Children's Voices Singing Heroes library magical night launches in Fuzhou
en.summary: The second Children's Voices Singing Heroes library magical night event opened in Fuzhou, combining children's storytelling of hero narratives, red-themed reading, and interactive experiences for young participants and families.

en.title: Overseas Chinese merchants participate in service trade fair: exploring emerging markets and promoting connectivity
en.summary: The 2026 China International Services Trade Fair is taking place in Beijing, where participating overseas Chinese merchants report the event provides opportunities for service trade cooperation beyond traditional goods trading and supports global service trade development.

en.title: (Economic Observation) Western Regions Forge Ahead, Local Service Trade Shows Diverse Strengths
en.summary: China's 2026 International Service Trade Fair is being held in Beijing, where western regional enterprises showcase their service trade advantages and pursue differentiated strategies to expand into new overseas markets.

en.title: Indonesian passenger ferry with at least 240 people goes missing, rescue personnel deployed
en.summary: An Indonesian passenger ferry carrying at least 240 people went missing in the Java Sea, prompting authorities to launch a search and rescue operation.

stories.title: Mainland Chinese HKUST student loses HK$1 million to scammer posing as official

en.title: Mainland Chinese HKUST student loses HK$1 million to scammer posing as official
en.summary: A 19-year-old mainland Chinese student at Hong Kong University of Science and Technology lost approximately HK$1 million after receiving calls from someone impersonating a government official who falsely accused her of involvement in a criminal case and demanded payment as a guarantee.

en.title: World's first pterosaur museum opens in Hami, Xinjiang
en.summary: The world's first pterosaur museum opened in Hami, Xinjiang, with the Hami Pterosaur Museum and the Hami Pterosaur-Yadan National Geological Park officially unveiled on September 13.

en.title: 2026 China (Guangxi)-ASEAN "AI+Law" Application Innovation Competition launched
en.summary: China and ASEAN launched an artificial intelligence and legal services innovation competition in 2026 focusing on cross-border legal service challenges. Registration is open to mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, and ASEAN countries.

en.title: Ruijin, "cradle of the republic," spreads wings to create new horizons, marking 90 years since Long March victory
en.summary: Marking the 90th anniversary of the Long March victory, Ruijin in Jiangxi province, historically significant as the cradle of the Chinese Republic, is developing new opportunities and growth.

stories.title: Next-gen wealthy Hongkongers drop property for higher returns in deposits and hedge funds

en.title: Next-gen wealthy Hongkongers drop property for higher returns in deposits and hedge funds
en.summary: Affluent Hong Kong residents are shifting away from property investment toward bank deposits and hedge funds seeking better financial returns. The trend reflects changing investment preferences among the city's wealthy families.

stories.title: How AI tools are reshaping stock trading, investment research in China

en.title: How AI tools are reshaping stock trading, investment research in China
en.summary: Quantitative traders in China are increasingly using artificial intelligence tools to automate research and data analysis tasks. AI agents now help investors collect historical data and analyze market patterns to inform trading decisions more quickly than traditional manual methods.

stories.title: Taobao’s ‘ugly’ goods find a growing market among China’s young consumers

en.title: Taobao's 'ugly' goods find a growing market among China's young consumers
en.summary: Unconventional and quirky products have become increasingly popular with young Chinese consumers on Taobao, with cumulative sales exceeding 230 million yuan since the platform's 2020 Uglies Award launch celebrating creatively unusual goods.

stories.title: Private equity’s Fang Fenglei on investing in China, capital market reforms

en.title: Private equity's Fang Fenglei on investing in China, capital market reforms
en.summary: Fang Fenglei, chairman of Hopu Investments, has played a major role in shaping China's capital markets over three decades, including helping establish the country's first joint venture investment bank and facilitating listings of state-owned companies in Hong Kong.
